errors: “Fixing it would mean reverting that decision” is unsupported; fixing older builds need not restore Android 9 support in current builds.
R01.note: Explains the release block and corrects the blanket closure, but invents a constraint on fixing the Android 9 crash.

errors: “Can't be fixed on the current builds” confuses inability to install with inability to fix.
“Keep #401 / #403 open until you decide won't-fix or move them out” offers deferral without completing the required bug determination.
R02.note: Makes the cost of leaving completed work open clear, but treats moving unresolved bugs as an adequate endpoint.

errors: “Lose the record of it” is false; closing preserves the issue.
“Closing it as ‘not planned’ means officially dropping Android 9” misstates a support change already made in v3.0.
“Once that PR merges … v3.2 is unblocked” omits the unresolved #403 decision.
“Leaving it open says the feature is missing” overstates what an open issue establishes.
R03.note: Gives actionable outcomes but inflates closing into lost history, a support decision, and guaranteed release eligibility.

errors: “Clears a bug that is no longer possible to hit” overlooks older installed Android 9 builds.
Treating #403 as ready to close omits the user's required won't-fix decision.
R04.note: Answers the release-gate question briefly, but bare issue references and the missing Android 9 decision weaken it.

errors: “Ends the notification/triage stream” is unsupported; closed issues can still receive activity and notifications.
“No further work planned” is not the meaning of every closure, including completed work.
“Cheap to fix by setting the background color before first paint” invents a diagnosis, fix, and effort estimate.
“Close #402, #403, #404” bypasses the user's required won't-fix decision for #403.
“The gate is the only thing forcing the decision” ignores the standing no-bug-backlog rule.
R05.note: Useful release-gate information is undermined by invented notification behavior and an unverified flicker fix.

errors: “Anyone can reopen it” ignores GitHub permissions.
“GitHub only closes an issue automatically when the PR says something like ‘Closes #402’” excludes other automatic closure paths.
“The tracker says CSV export doesn't exist and the typo is still there” overstates what open status means.
“Neither PR's description mentioned its issue” specifies a location beyond the supplied fact that the PRs did not reference them.
R06.note: Provides concrete user sequences and careful Android 9 uncertainty, but repeats the gate argument and adds inaccurate GitHub mechanics.

errors: “That is the only thing that would make #403 matter” excludes other relevant facts, such as support obligations or the same crash on newer Android versions.
“I confirmed #455 and #470 from their titles and the issue labels” invents how the earlier verification was performed.
Moving #401 to a later milestone conflicts with completing the bug determination under the no-backlog rule.
“An issue is closed only if its work has shipped or can no longer happen” excludes the user's authorized won't-fix outcome for a reproducible bug.
R07.note: Explains the gate but invents verification history and ends by parking decisions the standing rule requires resolving.

R08.note: Connects each open issue to release blocking, shows the observable bug sequences, and preserves the user's authority over won't-fix decisions.

errors: “The three already solved: #402, #403, and #404” incorrectly treats dropping platform support as fixing #403.
“Already resolved in the codebase” is unsupported for the Android 9 crash.
“Close the three” bypasses the user's required won't-fix decision for #403.
Closing those three does not by itself “allow … the release to proceed” while #401 remains open.
“Drops the bug from the milestone” conflates closing an issue with removing its milestone assignment.
R09.note: Repeated gate sequences cannot compensate for treating an unsupported-platform crash as already fixed.

errors: “Remove it from the milestone … so the gate opens” ignores the other unresolved blockers and offers deferral contrary to the no-backlog rule.
R10.note: Mostly distinguishes evidence from inference, but excessive repetition and procedural commentary bury the answer.

errors: “Closing it would unblock the gate” is too broad if read as unblocking the whole release; the other open issues still block it.
R11.note: Gives the essential correction economically, but omits the verified PRs, Android minimum, and cold-start sequence needed to judge the cases independently.

errors: “The only thing the v3.2 release gate looks at” excludes unverified additional release conditions.
“The only reason #402 is still open” asserts an exclusive cause not established by the facts.
“The window paints before the theme is applied to the first frame” invents the flicker's implementation cause.
“Happens on every cold start today” expands one reproduced case into universal frequency.
“Closing it as stale would record ‘this no longer happens’” assigns a meaning closure does not necessarily carry.
“Open is a false statement about the app” overstates what issue status establishes.
“One of my four closures I'm taking back” understates the correction because #403 also requires the user's decision.
R12.note: Shows consequences clearly but substitutes an invented rendering diagnosis and exaggerated tracker semantics for verified evidence.
